# Plan: Enforce Theseus sub-agents, skill access and reviewer models

## Overview

In Theseus sessions some models run a checkpoint's whole build inline instead of dispatching a fresh sub-agent per build/fix step, sub-agents that ask for the `tha-theseus` skill get "not found" (the skill lives only as vendored files under `plugin/skills/`, never in Hermes's skill index), and reviewer calls can silently land on a model other than the session's configured reviewer models. The change turns the plugin's `theseus_review` tooling into a hard gatekeeper with reinforcement: builder steps are blocked inline and forced into `delegate_task` children, every tool result names the remaining gate reviewers and the exact next sub-agent to spawn, the vendored skill becomes loadable by name, and a review recorded on the wrong model is refused. All of it lives in the Memento plugin (`plugin/`); the vendored skill and `theseus.js` stay untouched.

## Approach

Anchor everything on the enforcement machinery that already works — the `pre_tool_call` hook (`plugin/sessions.py`) plus `blocks_record`/`review()` in `plugin/theseus.py`, which already force every review verdict through the `theseus_review` tool. Extend that pattern in three directions: (1) block `theseus record <CP> red|tests` when the caller is the orchestrator itself, so builder steps can only be recorded by a delegated child; (2) expose the vendored skill into the profile's skills directory so `skill_view('tha-theseus')` resolves for orchestrator and children; (3) compare each review call's actual model against the configured reviewer slot and refuse on mismatch. Every tool result (success and error) additionally carries a short reinforcement block — remaining gate reviewers, the next `delegate_task` brief to dispatch — which is the "reinforcement" channel. Rejected alternatives: prompt-only strengthening (the models already ignore the prose — that is the reported failure); editing the vendored skill text (`plugin/skills/` is synced by `pnpm sync:theseus`, "don't edit it by hand"); gating on transcript inspection to detect "did not read SKILL.md" (brittle; findability fixes the reported failure directly).

## Changes

All paths are under `/opt/data/profiles/coder/projects/memento-x-hermes/memento/.worktrees/quirky-puffin-1f20/`.

- `plugin/theseus.py` — the main work.
  - `ensure_skill()` (new): symlink `plugin/skills/tha-theseus` into the profile skills directory that `agent.skill_utils.get_all_skills_dirs()` picks up (fallback `get_hermes_home() / "skills"`), owned-and-replaced only when the link already points at our vendored dir; refresh keyed on the `VENDORED.json` commit (reuses `vendored()`); log-only failure otherwise. Called from `register()` and lazily from `handle()`.
  - `blocks_record` → `blocks(tool, args, caller, record)`: keep the existing manual-review regexes (`_MANUAL_RECORD`, `_MANUAL_COVERAGE`), add a `_BUILD_RECORD` regex (`theseus record <CP> red|tests`) blocked only when the caller is the orchestrator (see `sessions.py` entry), with a new `SUBAGENT_BLOCK` message naming `delegate_task` and the `builder.md` brief. Reuses `record_for`/`_parent_of` via `sessions`.
  - `review()`: model guard comparing the `_ask` result's `provider`/`model` (the `via` it already reads) against the chosen `clean_models` slot — one re-ask on the configured model, then refuse with configured-vs-actual; gate backstop refusing a review for a checkpoint whose provenance shows inline builder steps; sets the "fix round open" flag when gate-3 findings arrive.
  - `reinforce(snap, cp, gate)` (new): short block appended to every `handle()` result (success and error): gate reviewers still needed at the current fingerprint, whether the next step is a fresh fix-mode builder child (with the exact brief lines), skill name + paths.
  - `INSTRUCTIONS`: one added fixed line — builder steps run in fresh `delegate_task` children (build and each fix round), reviews only via `theseus_review`, and the skill loads by name `tha-theseus` and lives at `{skill}`.
- `plugin/sessions.py` — `_before_tool`'s Theseus branch passes `task_id`/`session_id` into `theseus.blocks` and persists provenance in the session record's `theseus` JSON (same column `set_theseus` writes): per-checkpoint builder child ids, inline-step violations, fix-round flag. Caller classification helper: caller is the orchestrator when its id equals `record["session_id"]` or a `state.db` parent walk shows it is that session's compression continuation (delegation children carry their own session row; verify the exact marker in `delegate_tool`/`hermes_state` during implementation).
- `plugin/skills/tha-theseus/` — untouched (vendored; changed only via `pnpm sync:theseus`).
- `plugin/tests/test_theseus_enforcement.py` (new; create `plugin/tests/` if absent) — unittest coverage per checkpoint below.
- `AGENTS.md` (memento root) — one line in the plugin/Theseus documentation where the mode is described; `plugin/README.md` does not mention Theseus, so it stays untouched.

## Checkpoints

### Checkpoint 1: Expose the tha-theseus skill by name
- Commit: `feat(theseus): make the tha-theseus skill findable by name`
- Steps: implement `ensure_skill()` and its call sites in `plugin/theseus.py` (link into the profile skills dir, replace only our own link, refresh on `VENDORED.json` change, log-only on failure); add the skill-name line to `INSTRUCTIONS`; tests asserting the link is created in a temp home, points at the vendored dir, and that registration works when linking fails.
- Done when: `python3 -m unittest plugin/tests/test_theseus_enforcement.py -v` passes with the symlink tests green, and a fresh agent asking for `tha-theseus` resolves it through the skills directory instead of "not found".

### Checkpoint 2: Builder steps only in delegate sub-agents
- Commit: `feat(theseus): run builder steps in delegate sub-agents`
- Steps: extend `blocks_record` into `blocks(tool, args, caller, record)` with the `red|tests` regex and orchestrator classification; add `SUBAGENT_BLOCK` (names `delegate_task`, `builder.md`, the inputs to hand over); pass caller ids from `sessions._before_tool` and write provenance/violations into `project_sessions.theseus`; tests for orchestrator blocked / child allowed, `visual --skip|--carry`, `begin`, `advance`, `learn`, `wait` unaffected, manual review recording still blocked for everyone, fix-round flag blocking a second `record tests` from the build child while findings are open.
- Done when: the unittest suite proves the block matrix above, and the module imports cleanly with no Hermes runtime present (pure unit seams).

### Checkpoint 3: Reviewer model guard and reinforcement
- Commit: `feat(theseus): verify reviewer models and reinforce the workflow`
- Steps: `_model_guard` in `review()` (compare `via` vs the configured slot, re-ask once, then refuse with configured-vs-actual and the config fix); gate backstop refusing reviews for checkpoints with inline-step violations; `reinforce()` appended to every `handle()` result including error JSON; tests with a stubbed `ctx.llm` covering mismatch refusal, re-ask then success, matching pass, backstop refusal, and reinforcement content in success and error results.
- Done when: the full unittest suite passes and a stubbed review run records `--via` matching the configured model only.

## Verification

- From the memento repo root: `python3 -m unittest plugin/tests/test_theseus_enforcement.py -v` (unittest, not pytest — the plugin's convention), plus `python3 -c "import plugin.theseus, plugin.sessions"` for an import smoke.
- Manual smoke on a Hermes host with the plugin and Node 20+ (check `GET /api/plugins/memento/theseus` info shows `ready`): open a Theseus project session in a scratch project; then (a) from a fresh sub-agent, resolve `tha-theseus` via the skills index; (b) as the orchestrator run `node <skill>/scripts/theseus.js record CP1 red` and see it blocked with the sub-agent message, then dispatch a `delegate_task` child and see the same command accepted; (c) set a reviewer model in the session's Theseus settings and confirm a review that lands on another model is refused naming both models; (d) confirm `theseus_review` results carry the reinforcement block naming the remaining reviewers (`b`, `look`, `behave`, …).
- Ship with `open_pull_request` on the memento repo (template `.github/pull_request_template.md`); no hermes-agent or app changes are expected.

## Risks and assumptions

Settled answers (from the clarify round): enforcement is hard — one fresh `delegate_task` child per builder step/fix round and one `theseus_review` call per gate reviewer, with the hook blocking inline builder records and the tool refusing gates after inline steps; "missing the main skill" means sub-agents ask for `tha-theseus` and get "not found"; "wrong model" means reviewer calls silently landing on a model other than the configured slot; strictness is hard refusal plus reinforcement text in every tool result.

Decisions made without the user:

- Model mismatch policy: re-ask once on the configured model, then refuse the verdict — a verdict is never recorded from a wrong model.
- Caller classification is fail-open: `record red|tests` is blocked only when the caller is provably the orchestrator (its own session id or a compression continuation); unclassifiable callers pass, so a mis-detection can never trap a run. - Fix-round freshness is tracked in `project_sessions.theseus` (builder child per checkpoint; gate-3 findings open a fix round that the build child may not record). - On Hermes versions where `ctx.llm` results carry no `provider`/`model`, the guard passes with a note (fail-open) instead of refusing valid reviews.
- `plugin/skills/tha-theseus/**` and `theseus.js` are never hand-edited; enforcement lives in plugin code and the run instructions. `plugin/README.md` stays untouched (it does not document Theseus).
- Runs already in flight keep working; violations are only recorded from the upgrade on and gate later reviews of the affected checkpoint.

arguments.body: ## Summary A reply can name an image with a `MEDIA:` tag — the shape Hermes's messaging adapters strip and send as a photo. Run events, run output and transcript rows keep that tag as text (only the chat-completions routes resolve it, to a data URL), so every image the agent returned showed up in Chat and Code Sessions as a literal `MEDIA:` line. This shows them: the plugin serves the file behind the bot's key and the app renders the tag as an inline image with tap-to-zoom, keeping the raw text whenever an image can't load. ## Changes - **Plugin** (`plugin/media.py`, `plugin/__init__.py`): `GET /api/plugins/memento/media?path=…` behind `unauthorized()` validates the path with Hermes's own `validate_media_delivery_path`, serves only raster images (`.png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .bmp`) up to 25 MB via `web.FileResponse`, and answers the plugin's error shape otherwise (404/403/413/415). `media` added to `info`'s features. Five unit tests in `plugin/tests/test_media.py`. - **Hermes client** (`app/src/lib/hermes.ts`, `app/src/lib/media-tags.ts`): `getPluginMedia` reads the bytes with the bot's key; `mediaImages` splits a reply's text into text and image parts (Hermes's `MEDIA_TAG_CLEANUP_RE` tag shape ported, fenced code blocks skipped); fetched images are cached as object URLs for the app session only. - **Chat** (`app/src/components/chat/media-image.tsx`, `markdown.tsx`, `message-item.tsx`): tags render inline in both the chat bubble and the plain session thread; tapping opens the app's `Popup` (bottom sheet on phones, centred dialog from tablet width). Markdown images render through the same component and `data:image/` URLs survive `urlTransform` (react-markdown's default drops them). A tag that can't load — missing file, over 25 MB, no plugin, or a plugin from before the `media` feature — stays visible as its `MEDIA:` text. Only assistant reply text is scanned, and stored messages stay byte-identical to the transcript. - **Mock and docs**: the mock serves a generated PNG for `chart.png` (404 in the plugin's error shape for `missing.png`), and saying "image" or "chart" makes the agent answer with one of each tag; AGENTS.md documents the behaviour and the new files. ## Screenshots | | Light | Dark | | ------ | ----- | ---- | | Phone | inline chart + `MEDIA:` fallback in the thread; tap opens the bottom sheet with the enlarged image | bottom sheet with the enlarged image, layout intact | | Tablet | inline chart + fallback in the thread | centred dialog with the enlarged image | ## How to test 1. `pnpm install && pnpm mock` in one terminal, `pnpm dev` in another 2. Open the app, pick the mock bot, send "image" 3. The reply shows the chart inline and `MEDIA:/var/tmp/memento-mock/missing.png` as visible text; tap the image to zoom (bottom sheet at 390px, dialog at ≥768px) 4. Repeat in a Code session thread (Code → a project → New session → "image"): the same, in the plain thread 5. `python3 -m unittest discover -s plugin/tests -t .` from the repo root (104 tests; needs `cryptography`, as the plugin now does for Web Push) ## Checklist - [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` pass - [x] Checked on a phone-sized and a tablet-sized viewport, in light and dark mode - [x] If the IndexedDB schema changed: bumped the Dexie version in `src/lib/db.ts` and checked that existing data still loads — no schema change (rendering only) - [x] If the Hermes API usage changed: checked against the Hermes source or docs, and updated `scripts/mock-hermes.mjs` to match — verified against `gateway/platforms/base.py` and `api_server*.py`; mock updated - [x] New images, icons, characters and fonts are original or properly licensed (no third-party characters or brand assets) — the mock's chart is generated - [x] No secrets, API keys or personal data in code, screenshots or fixtures - [x] README updated if setup, configuration or behaviour changed — no README changes needed (documented in AGENTS.md) ## Notes for reviewers - Tag matching is a port of Hermes's `MEDIA_TAG_CLEANUP_RE` (the app can't import gateway code, so it's kept in sync by hand), narrowed to the raster extensions the plugin serves — SVG and extensionless tags deliberately stay text. - Plugin routes need the Bearer key an `` can't send, so the app fetches with the key and shows an object URL (the same pattern as the Theseus captures). Nothing new is stored in Dexie. - A tag mid-sentence renders as its own image block between the text segments. - Rebased on `main` (27f71bb): the reply rendering's new segment structure carries the media parts per segment, `getPluginMedia` sits beside the queue API in `hermes.ts`, and the mock's media route beside the new push routes.
